query: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals on high-surface-area supports improves catalytic activity and durability while reducing consumption.
generation.intervention: Atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals
generation.conditions: Operation under standard automotive exhaust conditions
generation.mechanism: Increased dispersion and utilization of platinum-group metals
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% improvement in catalytic activity and 15% improvement in durability with 30% reduction in platinum-group-metal consumption
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 500-900°C and space velocity of 50,000-100,000 h^-1
generation.uncertainty: Lack of specific data on the effect of atomic layer deposition on platinum-group-metal consumption in automotive exhaust catalysts

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of catalytic activity, durability, and platinum-group-metal consumption between atomic layer deposition and conventional catalyst synthesis methods
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If atomic layer deposition does not result in at least 10% improvement in catalytic activity and 10% improvement in durability with 20% reduction in platinum-group-metal consumption, the hypothesis is falsified
